title: Federated Bank - Data residency & compliance discovery

Next steps: share security pack, SOC 2/ISO docs, deployment options matrix, and schedule technical deep dive / benchmarks.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Time: 11:00 AM ET
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Federated Bank - Head of Data Privacy), Tom Alvarez (CTO), Jamal Reed (Compliance), Priya Nair (Infra)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro, I'm Maya Chen, I'm the AE working with you, and Liam is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Liam: hi all, hi. we'll dig into your residency and compliance needs and try to map out Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options.
[00:20] Sara: thanks. short context — Federated Bank is expanding EU services next year and legal flagged data residency and logging constraints. we need to understand whether Redwood Hosted is viable or if we need Dedicated/Private.
[00:34] Tom: yes, we run most infra on AWS eu-west-1 but we have strict audit rules; some logs are not allowed to leave our VPC.
[00:44] Liam: understood. first off, quick clarification on terminology: Hosted means requests and logs flow through Redwood's control plane and infrastructure; Dedicated is reserved capacity in our cloud with isolation and more control; Private is customer-managed control plane, can be VPC or on-prem.
[01:08] Sara: two main questions: one, can we keep EU user data in-region and not replicate to US? two, can we restrict or disable certain logs — audit and full transcripts — for regulatory reasons?
[01:22] Maya: good. yes, region pinning is supported; for Hosted customers we have EU-hosted endpoints and data residency commitments but it depends on plan and contractual terms. for the strictest controls we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[01:38] Jamal: when you say "data residency commitments" do you have SOC2 evidence and contractual clauses for not moving data? we need to show auditors.
[01:48] Maya: absolutely; we can share SOC 2 Type 2, ISO27001, and a data processing addendum (DPA) with EU data residency clauses. i'll attach those.
[01:58] Priya: about logs — our policy forbids storing full call transcripts in third-party logs for EU customers. is it possible to turn off request logging or store only redacted metadata?
[02:12] Liam: yes, we have configurable logging. by default the platform collects request metadata and traces, but you can disable request payload logging, mask PII, and configure retention windows. for Dedicated and Private deployments you can fully control logs and export them to your SIEM; for hosted the default retention is limited and we can negotiate different retention and deletion terms in contract.
[02:36] Tom: we also have KMS requirements — customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. is that possible in Hosted?
[02:46] Maya: Hosted supports provider-managed encryption by default. customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated customers; for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM and the keys never leave your environment.
[02:59] Sara: GDPR question: right to be forgotten — if a user requests deletion, how do you handle cached KV entries and logged prompts that might include personal data?
[03:12] Liam: we have a tiered approach: KV/prefix caches are configurable and can be tied to retention TTLs; for deletions we can purge relevant keys and scrub logs per the DPA. there's some operational coordination needed — we'll need a mapping from user identifiers to cache keys. for Hosted it's a coordinated request; for Dedicated/Private you can run automated deletion internally.
[03:38] Jamal: any issues with backups and replication? we can't have backups that accidentally replicate to non-EU regions.
[03:46] Liam: correct, backups can be limited to region and we support region-aware snapshot policies for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be scoped to EU regions but requires contractual guarantees. we'll include the backup/replication section in the security pack.
[04:05] Sara: HIPAA was mentioned by another team as an analogy — we don't process PHI as a bank typically, but some product lines touch health-related info. do you have experience with HIPAA controls?
[04:16] Maya: yes, while we're not a healthcare vendor per se, our platform supports HIPAA-like controls: encryption at rest/in transit, BAAs are available in enterprise contracts, enhanced audit logging, and access controls. we'll flag the relevant pages in the docs.
[04:28] Tom: one concern — certain logs contain PII and we can't have them logged for more than 30 days. can you do hard retention limits?
[04:37] Liam: yes. retention windows are configurable. for Hosted we can set short retention but need to verify with legal; Dedicated and Private give you deterministic control — you can enforce automatic deletion at 30 days.
[04:52] Priya: network — our security team wants VPC peering or private link and no public egress for inference traffic. can Redwood support private networking?
[05:02] Liam: yes, we offer VPC peering and private endpoints for Dedicated. Private deployments are inside your VPC/on-prem and meet that requirement. Hosted can use PrivateLink in some regions — depends on provider and configuration.
[05:18] Sara: audit logs — auditors ask for immutable logs and retention proof. does Redwood provide WORM-style logs or tamper evidence?
[05:28] Maya: our audit logs include immutability features and we can integrate with customer SIEMs; for Dedicated/Private you can forward logs to an S3 bucket with object lock or to your log provider to satisfy WORM requirements. we'll include patterns in the security pack.
[05:44] Tom: what about model artifacts and caching? some of our prompts could be sensitive; where are KV caches stored and are they encrypted?
[05:55] Liam: KV cache stored in-region and encrypted at rest. on Dedicated/Private you can control storage class and encryption keys; on Hosted it's encrypted with provider keys unless you opt for Dedicated with customer-managed KMS. also we provide options to limit cache retention and to disable persistent cache for sensitive workflows.
[06:16] Sara: any regulatory limitations around cross-border transfers for metadata? even though content is in EU, metadata sometimes goes to control plane in US for billing.
[06:27] Maya: that's a good point. in Hosted some metadata (for billing/telemetry) may be aggregated in our control plane; we can minimize or pseudonymize telemetry and provide contractual assurances. for full isolation Dedicated or Private is again recommended.
[06:43] Jamal: can you confirm whether full transcripts are ever used for model fine-tuning? we can't have customer content used to improve models unless explicitly opted in.
[06:53] Liam: yes, by default Redwood does not use customer prompts for model training. we have explicit opt-in for aggregated quality tuning and strict de-identification. we'll put the exact language in the DPA.
[07:06] Priya: operational question — if we run a pilot on Dedicated, how long is provisioning and what are the expected latencies compared to Hosted?
[07:18] Liam: Dedicated provisioning is typically a few days for reserved capacity, depending on region and GPU availability. latency is comparable; Dedicated can even reduce variance because of reserved pools. we'll share bench numbers for similar workloads.
[07:30] Tom: cost tradeoffs — we need a sense of unit costs and what controls drive price up (e.g., CMK, private link, extra retention).
[07:39] Maya: cost drivers: reserved capacity vs on-demand, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) add infra operational costs, private networking, and longer retention. we'll include a pricing delta sheet.
[07:51] Sara: for compliance we need an on-prem option for air-gapped workloads. does Redwood support a full on-prem package?
[08:00] Liam: yes, Private can be deployed on-prem and is designed for air-gapped environments, though it's a more involved engagement — we'll coordinate with professional services for that.
[08:12] Jamal: about logging restrictions — is there a way to redact PII automatically before logs leave our environment?
[08:20] Liam: there are pre-processing hooks and redaction pipelines; you can configure PII detection and masking client-side or in a private deployment to avoid external exposure.
[08:32] Maya: quick recap of options: Hosted (fast to launch, good for less-sensitive data, can be EU-hosted under contract), Dedicated (reserved capacity, CMK support, VPC/PrivateLink, stronger SLAs), Private (VPC/on-prem, full control, best for air-gapped/regulatory).
[08:53] Priya: next steps for us: we'll send the list of logs we cannot store, and the retention policies. we'd like the security pack and SOC2 docs. also schedule a 60-minute tech deep dive with Liam and our infra team next week.
[09:07] Maya: great — i'll send the security pack and SOC2/ISO reports, a deployment options matrix, and Dedicated pricing. Liam will follow up to schedule the technical deep dive.
[09:14] Tom: would be helpful to see a short benchmark — token throughput and p95 latency for a 2k context with batching enabled.
[09:22] Liam: noted — we'll provide a benchmark report and propose a pilot run.
[09:28] Sara: any blockers from our side — we need confirmation that full transcripts aren't used for tuning and the contractual deletion commitments.
[09:36] Maya: we'll include explicit contractual language in the DPA and follow up on deletion procedures.
[09:42] Jamal: thanks, that covers my concerns.
[09:45] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll circulate notes and next steps.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard terms (e.g., KV cache heard as 'KV cash'), minor name misspellings in automated transcript.
